newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OSCE head says Bosnians must forget, look forward.
newsitem.headline: OSCE head says Bosnians must forget, look forward.

text.p: Bosnia's deeply split ethnic groups should forgive and forget as West Europeans did after World War Two, the chairman of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) urged on Wednesday.

Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti, who holds the rotating annual OSCE chairmanship, made his appeal by quoting from a major speech delivered by British wartime premier Winston Churchill 50 years ago in Zurich.
Cotti said that Churchill, in unveiling his ideas for a "United States of Europe", urged Europeans to unite rather than harbour retributions and hatred against defeated Germany.

"Without an "act of faith' in the Bosnian family it will hardly be possible for reconciliation and peace to come," Cotti said in a ceremony marking the anniversary of Churchill's famous "Let Europe arise" address.
Churchill used the phrase "act of faith" in his speech of September 19,1946, to describe a willingness to overcome the pain of war, especially between France and Germany.

"If Europe is to be saved from infinate misery, and indeed from final doom, there must be this act of faith in the European family and this act of oblivion against all the crimes and follies of the past," Chruchill said.
Cotti has been closely linked to Bosnian peace efforts. The OSCE supervised Bosnia's first free elections under the 1995 Dayton Accord, which ended 43 months of war.
